title: The Day London Was Hit by a Flood of Beer

scenes.narration: In 1814, London was hit by a massive flood.
But it wasn't water.
It was beer.
On October 17th, workers at the Horse Shoe Brewery noticed something worrying.
One of the iron rings holding together a gigantic wooden beer vat had snapped.
That wasn't completely unusual. So they planned to repair it later.
Then, about an hour afterward...
the entire vat burst.
Hundreds of thousands of gallons of porter exploded through the brewery.
The force smashed other vats and blew through a brewery wall.
Then a wave of dark beer surged into the crowded neighborhood of St Giles.
People had almost no warning.
The flood crashed into buildings, filled basements, and buried people beneath wreckage.
Eight people were killed.
And somehow, the story got even stranger.
Afterward, reports said some residents collected the beer from the streets in whatever containers they could find.
The brewery was taken to court.
But the disaster was ultimately ruled an accident—described at the time as an "Act of God." The company wasn't held responsible for the deaths.
The Horse Shoe Brewery continued operating for more than a century after the disaster. And today, part of the site is occupied by London's Dominion Theatre.
So underneath one of London's busiest neighborhoods is the site of one of history's strangest disasters: the day a brewery unleashed a deadly flood of beer.
